licenses.externalSources: External photographs, artist GLBs and databases retain their source licenses. See ASSET-LICENSES.md and manifests.

baseHeader.methodology: Source-linked original summaries and reference-guided educational reconstructions. Models and motion are unvalidated; artist titles do not independently verify taxonomy. Navigation groups are not a universal kingdom system. Microbial behavior depends on strain and conditions. Expansion entries are individually referenced authored morphology studies; legacy Protista/Monera reporting categories do not replace modern domains. Actual screenshots, software checks and draft status are distinct from independent scientific validation.

before.summary: An adaptable canid. Small mammals are important prey, with other animal and plant foods also used.

behaviors.label: Walk
behaviors.description: An independently authored lateral four-beat walk in place. Sampled source soles retain stance contact and swing clearance while creator segment lengths remain fixed. Speeds, forces, pressure and animal trajectories are uncalibrated.

behaviors.label: Trot
behaviors.description: An authored grounded diagonal-pair trot in place on the retained creator skeleton. The primary study distinguishes trotting from slower food search; cycle timing, speed, limb paths and forces are not measured data.
behaviors.evidence: Primary behavioral context; independently authored qualitative gait

rendering.reason: Same source rig and coat through diagonal support/recovery; no calibrated animal trajectory or dynamics.

behaviors.label: Forage
behaviors.description: Supported head lowering and sensory search illustrate part of foraging. No prey grasp, chewing, swallowing or food intake is simulated.

behaviors.label: Jump
behaviors.description: Red foxes can pounce on small prey. Pouncing remains pending on this model; no jump substitute is shown.

rendering.reason: Species-specific pounce rig and contact sequence still need review on this retained textured surface.

behaviors.label: Rest posture
behaviors.description: The artist’s original recumbent posture on the same textured surface. It is a qualitative resting pose, not a physiological sleep simulation.

sources.title: University of Michigan · Animal Diversity Web
sources.scope: Species account: written natural history and biological processes. It does not validate the 3D model.

sources.title: Wikimedia Commons photographic reference
sources.scope: Photograph or micrograph, specimen caption and asset attribution; not a validation of the 3D model

sources.title: Yuk et al. (2024) · Effect of skull morphology on fox snow diving
sources.scope: Printed skull drop experiments and impact modeling. Relevant to written mousing context; no living-fox gait, full-body pounce or displayed artist-model validation. No figures, paper text, skull files, forces or trajectories imported.

sources.title: Yuk and Jung (2024) · Reply on skull impact and rotation
sources.scope: Pale-fox skull drop and added mass, rather than a living red fox. The reply identifies missing front-paw, soft-tissue and open-jaw effects. No data or images imported; it does not validate this model.

sources.title: Painter et al. (2016) · Red-fox behavioral bio-logging
sources.scope: Publisher methods/results and supplementary captions: two adult male rescued, captive-raised red foxes; trotting, foraging and trained mousing-like leaps in different enclosures. Supports qualitative behavior distinctions, not this generic mesh or its authored timing/footfall paths. Classifier accuracy is not animation validation; magnetic-cue mechanisms remain hypotheses. Video links were exposed, but the web reader cannot render QuickTime media.

visual.fidelity: The retained artist fox now has smoother back/tail contours and finer original coat cues. Walk uses separate lateral support phases; Trot uses diagonal limb pairs with grounded stance and lifted recovery on the same creator rig. Head search and creator-authored recumbent Rest remain available. Artist phenotype, facial/digit detail, tissue shape, timings, speed and biomechanics need specialist validation; pouncing and prey handling are still pending.
visual.scale: normalized display size; not a measurement
visual.description: Same credited textured fox across behaviors. Walk shows a qualitative four-beat gait with paw support; Forage shows supported head lowering and sensory search; Rest retains the artist’s original recumbent pose. The generic artist model is interpreted as a red fox, with unknown sex, population and life stage. Pouncing, prey capture, ingestion and physiological sleep are not modeled.

modelAsset.title: Fox
modelAsset.author: Alexei Ostapenko (https://sketchfab.com/alexanders823)
modelAsset.delivery: Bundled GLB; one local viewer across behaviors
modelAsset.biology: Generic artist Fox interpreted as a red fox by coat, muzzle, ears and proportions. Not a scanned or specialist-verified Vulpes vulpes specimen; sex, population and life stage are unknown.
modelAsset.changes: Original GLB bytes, two surfaces, source UV/image textures and 40-joint skeleton retained. Viewer samples the stable standing section at 19 seconds of the artist clip as its neutral pose and retains the original artist bind pose for quiet repose. Independently authored four-beat in-place walk uses original limb chains, bending poles, source paw orientation and displayed sole contacts; head-lowering/search illustrates only one component of foraging. No pouncing, prey grasp, ingestion, sleep physiology or validated animal trajectories are simulated. The full source waking clip remains in the bundled GLB; the viewer does not loop its abrupt end reset. v0.4.7: approximate anatomical-region links follow original posed surface vertices and existing morphs; source GLB bytes/materials/rig and behavioral deformation are unchanged. v0.5.6: The retained artist fox now has smoother back/tail contours and finer original coat cues. Walk uses separate lateral support phases; Trot uses diagonal limb pairs with grounded stance and lifted recovery on the same creator rig. Head search and creator-authored recumbent Rest remain available. Artist phenotype, facial/digit detail, tissue shape, timings, speed and biomechanics need specialist validation; pouncing and prey handling are still pending. Viewer body mesh receives one conservative trunk/tail subdivision; original face/toe vertices, original UV samples and 40-joint creator skeleton remain. Added edge UV/skin interpolation and normals are authored derivatives.
